IP Address

You might say

Why can I open the page on my computer but others cannot?

A network-layer address used to locate an interface and route data·In local development, 127.0.0.1 is the current device's loopback interface; a LAN address is reachable only within its routed network. Sharing localhost with a coworker still points to their own computer. A public IP alone does not mean anyone can connect: routing, ports, service listening, and access rules also matter.
Know first
Port
IP AddressIP
Who can reach each kind of address
localhost:3000
Loopback addressPoints to the device making the request
Dev service on the computerService computer · 192.168.1.20:3000
Computer browser →localhost:3000 → the computer's own loopback interface
Can open: this example service runs on this computer
Phone browser →localhost:3000 → the phone's own loopback interface
Fails: this example phone is not running the dev service

localhost always points to the device making the request. In this example the dev service runs on the computer and listens on its local port; the phone is not running it, so the phone's localhost cannot reach the computer.

The dev service runs on the computer at 192.168.1.20:3000 on the LAN; localhost points to whichever device makes the request.

Address scope decides who can reach it

127.0.0.1: only this machine: localhost and 127.0.0.1 mean this very computer; anyone else using the address reaches their own machine.

LAN address: routed within a network: Private addresses such as 192.168.x.x and 10.x.x.x can be routed within their network; the service must also listen on a reachable interface, and firewall and network rules must allow the connection.

A public address: potentially reachable from the internet: A public address can be routed from the internet, but connections still depend on ports, service listening, firewalls, and other access rules; a domain name resolves to an address.

What people often confuse

Listening address and access address are two things: if the service listens on localhost only, even giving a colleague the LAN address fails. When others cannot reach it, check the listening scope first, then the address type.

You can say this to an AI Agent

The local service runs on localhost:3000 and my colleague cannot reach it. Tell me this machine's LAN address and confirm the dev server listens on all interfaces rather than localhost only; if public access is needed, explain where to deploy.
